notes: Poly Studio X50 is an all-in-one 4K video conferencing bar (camera + stereo speakers + mic array + onboard Poly Video OS codec) for small/mid-sized rooms; no separate room PC/Mac required. Poly's own product URL (poly.com/us/en/products/video-conferencing/studio/studio-x50) now 301-redirects to the newer replacement model "Studio X52" on hp.com, so the live manufacturer product page no longer documents the X50. I instead used the official Poly-branded PDF datasheet ("(c)2023 Poly", doc 1499379), mirrored on Polycom's Taiwan site (polycom.com.tw/file/studio-x50-ds-en.pdf); content is identical to the earlier 2022 edition of the same Poly datasheet, cross-checked via a second copy (av-iq.com mirror). Not included as a distinct port: "Input for optional expansion microphone" (p/n 2200-69631-001) — this is a real documented port but its exact connector type could not be confirmed from available sources, so it was omitted rather than guessed. HDMI version (1.4/2.0/2.1) and USB-C speed are not stated anywhere in Poly's materials, so grades were omitted per instructions rather than inferred. Physical size: 30 x 4 x 4 in (762 x 102 x 102 mm), 5.6 lb/2.54 kg — desktop/shelf/wall-mount unit, not rack-mountable (VESA mount kit and stand available as options), hence rackUnits omitted. Sold in bundles with an optional Poly TC8/TC10 touch controller.

ports.name: HDMI In
ports.note: Content/laptop input; datasheet also lists a 1x HDMI audio input which is the same physical port.

ports.name: USB-C
ports.note: Used for BYOD/USB device mode; speed grade not stated by Poly.

ports.name: Power
ports.note: Ships with an external auto-sensing power supply (37 VA @ 120V/60Hz or 230V/50-60Hz). Exact device-side connector shape is not pictured in the sourced datasheet, so dc-barrel is used as the closest standard match rather than a visually confirmed connector.
